draft.title: Policies on emissions
card: Governments respond to emissions at local, national and international levels. Each response tries to cut emissions at the lowest cost to the economy.
Carbon price
a charge on each tonne of greenhouse gas emitted. It makes emitting cost more, so firms look for the cheapest ways to cut back.
Subsidy
a payment from government that lowers the cost of clean energy, such as rooftop solar. It makes clean options cheaper to buy.
Regulation
a rule that sets a limit or standard, such as a cap on emissions from power stations. Firms that break it can be fined.
draft.remember: Policies cut emissions by making them costlier, making clean energy cheaper, or setting rules.

a.q: Which policy works by making each tonne of emissions cost the emitter more?
a.why: A carbon price is a charge on each tonne emitted, so emitting costs more. A subsidy works the other way, by making clean energy cheaper rather than making emissions dearer.
a.clue: Which one is a charge per tonne?

b.q: The Victorian Government pays households part of the cost of installing rooftop solar panels. What type of policy is this?
b.why: A payment that lowers the cost of clean energy is a subsidy. It is not a carbon price, because it does not charge anyone for emitting. It is not a regulation, because it sets no rule or limit.
b.clue: Is the government paying, charging or making a rule?

problems.detail: Two distractors, 'A payment for rooftop solar' and 'A clean energy subsidy', describe the same policy. A student can rule both out together, because they cannot both be the single right answer, so the question is easier than it looks.

proposal.title: Policies on emissions
card: Governments respond to emissions at local, national and international levels, each aiming to cut emissions at the lowest cost. In a global agreement, such as the Paris Agreement, countries set targets to cut their emissions.
Carbon price
a charge on each tonne of greenhouse gas emitted. It makes emitting cost more, so firms look for the cheapest ways to cut back.
Subsidy
a payment from government that lowers the cost of clean energy, such as rooftop solar. It makes clean options cheaper to buy.
Regulation
a rule that sets a limit or standard, such as a cap on emissions from power stations. Firms that break it can be fined.
proposal.remember: Policies cut emissions by making them costlier, making clean energy cheaper, setting rules or agreeing on targets.

a.why: A carbon price is a charge on each tonne emitted, so emitting costs more. A subsidy works the other way, by making clean energy cheaper rather than making emissions dearer. A standard sets a limit, and a global agreement sets targets, but neither charges per tonne.
a.clue: Which one is a charge per tonne?

b.q: The Victorian Government pays households part of the cost of installing rooftop solar panels. What type of policy is this?
b.why: A payment that lowers the cost of clean energy is a subsidy. It is not a carbon price, because it does not charge anyone for emitting. It is not a regulation, because it sets no rule or limit, and it is a state policy, not a deal between countries.
b.clue: Is the government paying, charging or making a rule?
